rows.evidence: Q1: Abstract and Sections III-V report the authors' own development of an irrigation automation platform (sensor modules, controllers, servers, three scheduling modalities) and software testing.
rows.notes: The paper is a system-design/engineering description. It reports no crop yield or quality measurements, no drought-condition trial and no field outcome data of any kind; it only describes the hardware/software architecture and proposed scheduling modes. The claim that automated sensor-based systems maintained constant yield and quality under drought is not supported by any result in this study.

rows.evidence: Q1: Abstract and Sections III-V report the authors' own development of the platform and software testing.
rows.notes: No drought-risk or yield-stability outcome is measured. The study describes a monitoring/control architecture (sensors, valve control, pumps, GPRS, servers) and proposes closed-loop and open-loop scheduling modes; it reports no operation under drought and no yield/quality data. Only the existence of the system (a precondition) is shown.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections II-V describe the authors' own three-layer architecture, integrated sensor module (Fig. 2), renewable-energy control subsystem, Lorentz solar pumps, and reporting applications (Fig. 6); abstract states software testing was carried out.
rows.notes: The study shows that a platform integrating renewable energy, remote control and report visualization was built, but reports no measurement of water saved or irrigation efficiency achieved. Fig. 6 is an example report diagram of irrigation norms, precipitation and volumes, not an evaluation result. Statements that closed-loop control 'ensures optimal water consumption' are assertions, not findings. Supports only a precondition of water conservation.

rows.evidence: Q1: Section III and Fig. 2 report the authors' own integrated sensor module including soil humidity and temperature at two depths.
rows.notes: The study documents that a sensor module measuring soil humidity at two levels was designed and built, which matches the context sentence about monitoring at various depths. It reports no water-use-efficiency result from soil-moisture-based targeted irrigation and no field trial; grapes are never mentioned. Monitoring capability is a precondition, not the claimed water-conservation effect.

rows.evidence: Q1: Section III and Fig. 2 report the authors' own integrated sensor module with soil humidity/temperature sensors at two depths.
rows.notes: No grape or any crop quality/yield data are reported; the paper contains no agronomic trial. It only describes the sensor hardware and the scheduling/control modalities. The claim about improved grape quality is not supported by any result in this study.

notes: Conference paper (Secrieru et al. 2017) describing the design of a remote-control and monitoring platform for drip/sprinkler irrigation powered by wind/PV in Moldova. It is an engineering development report with no outcome measurements (water use, yield, quality, drought response). Figure text is partly in Romanian and figures are reproduced as garbled layout, but the narrative text appears complete.
